subject: Electrical Engineering
title: Latches: Remembering One Bit
description: A 60-second lesson on Latches: Remembering One Bit.

hook.text: Logic gates forget — change the input and the output changes instantly. Memory needs something more.

buildup.text: Cross-connect two NOR gates and the output stays put even when the input changes. Memory.

discovery.text: This SR latch has Set and Reset inputs. Set makes it store 1. Reset makes it store 0.

twist.text: Setting both S and R to 1 is forbidden — the output becomes unpredictable.

climax.text: Latches are the simplest memory elements — the foundation of registers and RAM.

punchline.text: Two gates feeding back into each other — the tiniest memory in digital logic.

quiz.question: What makes an SR latch different from a simple gate?
options: It can add two numbers together
Its feedback loop lets it hold a value even after the input changes
It uses three or more inputs instead of two
